about.title: Vacaville Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Vacaville sits where I-80 splits the distance between Sacramento and the Bay Area, and much of that traffic never stops. In 2025, the city recorded 335 injury collisions, with 463 people hurt and one life lost. Those are public counts, not warnings, but they help explain why so many local residents find themselves dealing with an adjuster on a Friday afternoon, when reported crashes here cluster between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m. Alamo Drive, Peabody Road, and Nut Tree Road appear most often in the collision records alongside the interstate. If you were hurt on any of them, a few early decisions matter. Get medical care and keep every receipt. Photograph the vehicles before they are moved. Politely decline to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement until you have spoken with a lawyer. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service connecting Vacaville residents with an independent personal injury attorney who takes Solano County cases on contingency, meaning no attorney fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Vacaville Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: You Don't Lose Your Claim Over a Missed Date
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim involving a city, county, or Caltrans vehicle or roadway can carry a deadline as short as six months. The attorney you're connected with sorts out which clock applies before it runs.

items.title: Partial Blame Doesn't Mean Zero Recovery
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if an insurer argues you share some responsibility for the crash. Your share of fault reduces the recovery rather than erasing it.

items.title: No Fee Unless There Is a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is nothing to pay up front and no attorney fee if the case does not result in a recovery. Our connection service is free as well.

items.question: I was rear-ended on I-80 near the Nut Tree exit. Does it matter that it happened on the freeway?
items.answer: It can. Freeway crashes are usually investigated by the California Highway Patrol rather than Vacaville police, so your collision report will come from a different agency. If a state vehicle or a roadway defect played a part, a government claim with a much shorter deadline may be involved. An attorney can request the right report and evaluate every potentially responsible party.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling. Should I give them a statement?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is generally wise to wait until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may ask questions designed to minimize your injuries or shift fault onto you. Notify your own insurer of the crash, but keep conversations with the other side brief and unrecorded.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering in California?
items.answer: For a standard car accident claim against a private driver, California places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. The value depends on the evidence, the severity of your injuries, and how your life has been affected. An attorney can help document these losses, but no one can promise a specific result.
